title: Microburst runway recon & hiring gateways — sensitivity snapshot
body:
Purpose:
This memo is a short, executable snapshot for the finance + GTM + people partnership to (1) reconcile runway under 2 microburst pricing/demand shocks, (2) define hard hiring gateways and quick-switchover levers, and (3) capture the minimal spreadsheet cells and assumptions needed for rapid re-run by ICs.

Context and why this is different:
- We've seen increasing variance in token mix (embedding-heavy customers vs gen-heavy) that amplifies short-term token-revenue volatility.
- Operationally we have a small pool of reserved GPU capacity (Dedicated) and a larger hosted tail; pricing changes that tilt customers between those two modes can swing near-term margin and cash by several percent.
- This doc is short-form: not a full model. It provides 2 explicit microburst scenarios, clear hiring gates, and a prioritized action list to implement in <72h.

Key model cells (spreadsheet locations referenced by tab/cell for the canonical workbook 'microburst-sensitivity-2026.xls'):
- Assumptions tab: A2: Base monthly revenue (hosted + dedicated) = $11,400,000
- Assumptions tab: A3: Gross margin (hosted weighted) = 62%
- Token mix tab: B2: % of tokens billed as generation (gen %) = 46% (base)
- Cost tab: C5: Avg GPU direct cost / token (gen) = $0.00032; C6: Avg GPU direct cost / token (embed) = $0.00005
- Headcount tab: H2: FTE = 148; H3: monthly OpEx people = $1,320,000
- Runway calc tab: R3: cash balance = $153,000,000; R4: monthly net burn = OpEx + infra net of revenue

Microburst scenarios (assumptions and outputs):
1) Demand-contraction & price-compression (Short cold-snap) — 3-month window
   - Assumptions: Revenue down 22% in month 1, then -14% month 2, -8% month 3 (stabilizes afterwards). Price competition causes an effective blended price drop of 12% for new customers (retrofit effect applied to 30% of churn-prone customers).
   - Token mix: gen% slides from 46% to 41% as customers postpone gen workloads.
   - Direct infra cost delta: -7% (less volume) but margin hit on committed Dedicated pools where utilization drops.
   - Output (spreadsheet snapshot): 3-month cumulative cash delta = -$18.1M vs base; runway shortened by 2.3 months (from 30.2 to 27.9).

2) Pricing shock + burst shift to dedicated (Capacity mismatch) — 2-month acute window
   - Assumptions: A major partner (top-10 customer) renegotiates to a lower unit price (-28%) and moves 40% of its traffic onto dedicated reserved pools for latency guarantees. Several SMB customers shift from hosted to cheaper alternatives, net hosted revenue -11% month 1 and -4% month 2.
   - Token mix: gen% increases to 53% for partner traffic (higher-latency gen use), overall gen% +3 points.
   - Infra cost delta: reserved pools increase fixed cost burden (we pay reserved lease regardless of utilization) -> effective margin compression from 62% to 52% in month 1.
   - Output: immediate 2-month cash pressure of -$12.6M; if hiring continues unchanged runway reduces by 1.6 months.

Headcount and hiring gateways (hard triggers we can implement immediately):
- Gateway 1 (Immediate hiring freeze): Trigger if 3-month rolling projected net cash delta <= -$10M. Action: freeze all non-clinical hiring and pause contractor-to-hire conversions.
- Gateway 2 (Elastic contractor augmentation): Trigger if revenue drop >15% and Dedicated underutilization >20% for 2 consecutive weeks. Action: convert 40% of open requisitions to short-term contractors only with 30-day notice.
- Gateway 3 (Selective deferral): Trigger if runway compression >1.5 months vs baseline. Action: defer open engineering hiring except for security/SRE and ops critical roles; allow product/SDR hiring to continue at 30% of plan.
- Gateway 4 (Acceleration to preserve revenue): Trigger if churn risk score for top-30 customers increases by >10 points in 30 days. Action: enable targeted headcount hires (2x AMs) and $200k temporary retention / credit offers.

Pricing sensitivity levers (fast to deploy):
- Short-term promotional credits: cap to 6% of hosted MRR; deploy only to churn-score > 55 customers.
- Temporary tiered price floors: increase per-token minimum price for new customers on low-commit slabs by 8%; communicate as temporary market-alignment.
- Commitment reprice for dedicated pools: grandfather existing reserved customers for 60 days, then introduce a utilization-band surcharge if utilization <45%.
- Per-route surcharge: small (0.5–1.5%) premium for ultra-low-latency routes during high utilization windows.

Operational & accounting notes (things to reconcile with SRE / legal):
- CapEx vs OpEx recognition for reserved GPU contracts — if we defer purchases, legal needs 72h to update vendor notices.
- Deferred revenue effects: promotional credits reduce recognized revenue; need to flag in monthly close under 'revenue reductions' bucket.
- Payroll timing: non-exempt contractor freezes affect P&L immediately; salary freezes recognized next payroll cycle.

Priority short-list (implement within 72 hours if scenario triggers):
1) Finance: open 'microburst-sensitivity-2026.xls', set scenario tab to Scenario A (copy cells A2:A12), push recalculation and distribute to CFO + head of GtM. (Owner: Maya)
2) People Ops: implement hiring freeze email template and publish on internal portal; prepare list of 'critical hires' (security/SRE/product ops) to carve out. (Owner: Priya)
3) Sales/GTM: flag top-30 churn-risk customers and prepare two credit templates: retention-credit and usage-smoothing-credit. (Owner: Liam)
4) Engineering Ops: run utilization delta report for dedicated pools (72h window) and provide weekly snapshot. (Owner: Carlos)

Open questions and follow-ups (for the 1-week working group):
- How sensitive is churn to a 6% promotional credit vs an 8% price-floor? (GTM-run A/B)
- Do we have contractual levers in our Dedicated T&Cs to apply utilization surcharges? (Legal)
- What is the break-even point for converting a contractor-to-hire under this model (assume 20% hiring fee premium)? (People Ops + Finance)

Appendix: quick sensitivity table (snapshot values, canonical workbook cells in parentheses)
- Base monthly net cash change: +$1.9M (Runway!R10)
- Scenario 1 month 1 delta: -$3.7M (Scen1!D4)
- Scenario 1 cumulative 3-mo delta: -$18.1M (Scen1!E10)
- Scenario 2 immediate 2-mo delta: -$12.6M (Scen2!C7)
- Hiring freeze threshold cell: Runway!S6 = -10,000,000

Notes to self: keep this doc compact and re-run numbers after the March 5 billing close. If we start seeing reserved pool utilization <55% for >10 days, escalate to exec.

Quick checklist before distribution:
- [ ] Attach recalculated workbook export (PDF) to the exec summary
- [ ] Get legal confirmation on Dedicated surcharge language
- [ ] People Ops to tag critical hires and update CarveOut spreadsheet
- [ ] GTM to prepare customer communication templates

End of snapshot.
